constraints.snippet: The average active power ramp rate of the large load, measured over a rolling 10-minute interval, shall not exceed 20 MW/min.
constraints.notes: Applies to normal operating conditions, including routine operational changes, startup, shutdown, and restoration following outages; does not apply to automatic responses to faults or disturbances for equipment protection or fault ride-through.

constraints.snippet: ATC: Any active power change greater than 50 MW must be limited to a ramp rate of less than 0.5 MW/s (30 MW/min).
constraints.notes: Applies only to active power changes > 50 MW; 0.5 MW/s = 30 MW/min.

constraints.snippet: Southern Company: 20 MW/min. In addition, the top quartile (P75) of active power ramp rate, as averaged across consecutive 1-minute periods, should also not exceed 20 MW/min.
constraints.source_section: 2.4. Ramp Rate Limit - Industry Practice (Southern Company)

constraints.snippet: ATC and SPP: Require active power variations to remain below 25 MW over a 5-second interval.
constraints.source_section: 3.1 Low Frequency Cycling - Industry Practice (ATC and SPP)

constraints.snippet: Southern Company: Requires active power variations to remain below 10 MW over a 4–6 second interval.
constraints.source_section: 3.1 Low Frequency Cycling - Industry Practice (Southern Company)

constraints.snippet: ERCOT: Have proposed limiting active power variations to less than 10 MW over a 5-second interval.
LIPA: Requires frequency-domain content in the 0.1–5 Hz range to remain below 10 MW and content in the 5–55 Hz range to remain below 3.5 MW.
